nodes.name: Code refutation after substitution
nodes.lean:
let D : ℕ → Prop := fun φ : ℕ ↦
    IsSemiformula ℒₒᵣ 1 φ ∧ T.Provable (neg ℒₒᵣ <| subst ℒₒᵣ ?[numeral φ] φ)
  have D_re : REPred D := by
    have : 𝚺₁-Predicate fun φ : ℕ ↦
        IsSemiformula ℒₒᵣ 1 φ ∧ T.Provable (neg ℒₒᵣ <| subst ℒₒᵣ ?[numeral φ] φ) := by
      definability
    exact re_iff_sigma1.mpr this
  have D_spec (φ : Semisentence ℒₒᵣ 1) : D ⌜φ⌝ ↔ T ⊢ ∼φ/[⌜φ⌝] := by
    simp [D, ←provable_iff_provable, Sentence.quote_def,
      Rewriting.emb_subst_eq_subst_coe₁, Semiformula.quote_def]

nodes.name: Show D is recursively enumerable
nodes.lean:
have D_re : REPred D := by
    have : 𝚺₁-Predicate fun φ : ℕ ↦
        IsSemiformula ℒₒᵣ 1 φ ∧ T.Provable (neg ℒₒᵣ <| subst ℒₒᵣ ?[numeral φ] φ) := by
      definability
    exact re_iff_sigma1.mpr this

nodes.name: Represent D by a formula
nodes.lean:
let δ : Semisentence ℒₒᵣ 1 := codeOfREPred D
  have (n : ℕ) : D n ↔ T ⊢ δ/[↑n] := by
    simpa [Semiformula.coe_subst_eq_subst_coe₁] using re_complete D_re

nodes.name: Substitute δ’s own code
nodes.lean:
let π : Sentence ℒₒᵣ := δ/[⌜δ⌝]
  have : T ⊢ π ↔ T ⊢ ∼π := calc
    T ⊢ π ↔ T ⊢ δ/[⌜δ⌝]  := by rfl
    _     ↔ D ⌜δ⌝        := by simpa using (this ⌜δ⌝).symm
    _     ↔ T ⊢ ∼δ/[⌜δ⌝] := D_spec δ
    _     ↔ T ⊢ ∼π       := by rfl

refine incomplete_def.mpr ⟨π, ?_, ?_⟩

nodes.name: Form standard provability
nodes.lean:
/-- The derivability condition D1. -/
theorem provable_D1 {σ} : T ⊢ σ → 𝗜𝚺₁ ⊢ □σ := fun h ↦
  provable_of_models _ _ fun (V : Type) _ _ ↦ by simpa [models_iff] using internalize_provability (V := V) h

/-- The derivability condition D2. -/
theorem provable_D2 {σ π} : 𝗜𝚺₁ ⊢ □(σ ➝ π) ➝ □σ ➝ □π :=
  provable_of_models _ _ fun (V : Type) _ _ ↦ by simpa [models_iff] using modus_ponens_sentence T

variable (T)

noncomputable abbrev _root_.LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvability : Provability 𝗜𝚺₁ T where
  prov := T.provable
  D1 := provable_D1

variable {T}

instance : T.standardProvability.HBL2 := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ provable_D2⟩

lemma standardProvability_def (σ : Sentence L) : T.standardProvability σ = T.provabilityPred σ := rfl

instance [T.Δ₁] : T.standardProvability.SoundOnModel ℕ :=
  ⟨fun {σ} ↦ by simp [Arithmetic.standardProvability_def, models_iff]⟩

nodes.name: Supply derivability conditions
nodes.lean:
simpa [models_iff] using Bootstrapping.Arithmetic.sigma_one_complete (T := T) (V := V) hσ

/-- The derivability condition D3. -/
theorem provable_D3 [𝗣𝗔⁻ ⪯ T] {σ : Sentence ℒₒᵣ} :
    𝗜𝚺₁ ⊢ □σ ➝ □□σ := provable_sigma_one_complete (by simp)

open LO.Entailment LO.Entailment.FiniteContext

variable {U : ArithmeticTheory}

lemma provable_D2_context [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ U] {Γ σ π} (hσπ : Γ ⊢[U] □(σ ➝ π)) (hσ : Γ ⊢[U] □σ) :
    Γ ⊢[U] □π := FiniteContext.of'! (weakening inferInstance provable_D2) ⨀! hσπ ⨀! hσ

lemma provable_D3_context [𝗣𝗔⁻ ⪯ T] [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ U] {Γ σ} (hσπ : Γ ⊢[U] □σ) :
  Γ ⊢[U] □□σ := FiniteContext.of'! (weakening inferInstance provable_D3) ⨀! hσπ

lemma provable_sound [U.SoundOnHierarchy 𝚺 1] {σ} : U ⊢ □σ → T ⊢ σ := fun h ↦ by
  have : ℕ ⊧ₘ T.provabilityPred σ := ArithmeticTheory.SoundOn.sound (F := Arithmetic.Hierarchy 𝚺 1) h (by simp)
  simpa [models_iff] using this

lemma provable_complete [U.SoundOnHierarchy 𝚺 1] [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ U] {σ} : T ⊢ σ ↔ U ⊢ □σ :=
  ⟨fun h ↦ weakening inferInstance (provable_D1 h), provable_sound⟩

instance [𝗣𝗔⁻ ⪯ T] : T.standardProvability.HBL3 := ⟨fun _ ↦ provable_D3⟩

instance [𝗣𝗔⁻ ⪯ T] : T.standardProvability.HBL where

nodes.lean:
variable [L.DecidableEq] [L.ReferenceableBy L] {T₀ T : Theory L} [T₀ ⪯ T] [Diagonalization T₀] [Consistent T]

variable (𝔅 : Provability T₀ T)

local notation "𝗚" => 𝔅.gödel

theorem unprovable_gödel : T ⊬ 𝗚 := by
  intro h;
  have h₁ : T ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 := D1_shift h
  have : T ⊢ ⊥ := by cl_prover [h₁, 𝔅.gödel_spec, h]
  have : ¬Consistent T := not_consistent_iff_inconsistent.mpr <|
    inconsistent_iff_provable_bot.mpr this
  contradiction

nodes.name: Formalize the implication
nodes.lean:
/-- Formalized First Incompleteness Theorem -/
theorem formalized_unprovable_gödel : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅.con ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 := by
  suffices T₀ ⊢ ∼𝔅 ⊥ ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 from this
  have h₁ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚) := 𝔅.D3 𝗚
  have h₂ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚 ➝ ⊥) := prov_distribute_imply <| by cl_prover [𝔅.gödel_spec]
  have h₃ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚 ➝ ⊥) ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚) ➝ 𝔅 ⊥ := 𝔅.D2 (𝔅 𝗚) ⊥
  cl_prover [h₁, h₂, h₃]

nodes.name: Relate G to consistency
nodes.lean:
lemma formalized_consistent_of_existance_unprovable (σ) : T₀ ⊢ ∼𝔅 σ ➝ 𝔅.con := contra! $ 𝔅.D2 _ _ ⨀ (𝔅.D1 efq!)

variable [T₀ ⪯ T] [Diagonalization T₀] (𝔅)

local notation "𝗚" => 𝔅.gödel

/-- Formalized First Incompleteness Theorem -/
theorem formalized_unprovable_gödel : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅.con ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 := by
  suffices T₀ ⊢ ∼𝔅 ⊥ ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 from this
  have h₁ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚) := 𝔅.D3 𝗚
  have h₂ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚 ➝ ⊥) := prov_distribute_imply <| by cl_prover [𝔅.gödel_spec]
  have h₃ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚 ➝ ⊥) ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚) ➝ 𝔅 ⊥ := 𝔅.D2 (𝔅 𝗚) ⊥
  cl_prover [h₁, h₂, h₃]

theorem gödel_iff_con : T₀ ⊢ 𝗚 ⭤ 𝔅.con := by
  have h₁ : T₀ ⊢ ∼𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅.con := formalized_consistent_of_existance_unprovable 𝗚
  have h₂ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅.con ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 := 𝔅.formalized_unprovable_gödel
  have h₃ : T₀ ⊢ 𝗚 ⭤ ∼𝔅 𝗚 := 𝔅.gödel_spec
  cl_prover [h₁, h₂, h₃]

nodes.name: Reduce a proof of consistency to G
nodes.lean:
theorem con_unprovable [Consistent T] : T ⊬ 𝔅.con := by
  intro h
  have : T₀ ⊢ 𝗚 ⭤ 𝔅.con := 𝔅.gödel_iff_con
  have : T ⊢ 𝗚 := by cl_prover [h, this]
  exact 𝔅.unprovable_gödel this

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.incomplete.title: First incompleteness theorem
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.incomplete.summary: Fix a Δ₁-presented, Σ₁-sound arithmetic theory T that proves the axioms of R₀. The proof constructs one sentence π for which either a proof or a refutation would give both, contradicting consistency. This specific witness establishes the existential assertion that every theory satisfying these hypotheses leaves some sentence undecided.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.incomplete.why_here: The constructed undecided sentence witnesses the theorem’s conclusion.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.consistent.title: Second incompleteness theorem
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.consistent.summary: Let T be a consistent, Δ₁-presented arithmetic theory extending IΣ₁. Its standard consistency sentence says, inside arithmetic, that there is no T-proof of contradiction. The proof shows that a T-proof of this sentence would yield a T-proof of a particular Gödel sentence, whose external unprovability follows from consistency.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.consistent.why_here: The root specializes the generic unprovability result to T’s standard arithmetic proof predicate.

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_iff_sig.title: Σ₁ and recursive enumerability
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_iff_sig.summary: A recursively enumerable predicate can be recognized by a search that eventually finds a witness for every positive case. A Σ₁ definition expresses just such existence of a finite witness that can be checked arithmetically. This equivalence lets the proof switch from a formula defining D to a representation of a recursively enumerable predicate.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_iff_sig.why_here: The proof applies the direction from Σ₁ definability to recursive enumerability to D.

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvab.title: Standard provability structure
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvab.summary: An expression such as □ₜφ is an arithmetic sentence about the Gödel code of φ. It asserts the existence of a code for a valid T-proof of φ. The standard structure packages this predicate with the facts needed to reason about it inside arithmetic.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvab.why_here: Unfolding the definition identifies the proof predicate and the internalization rule used in the arithmetic instance.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.consistent.title: Internal consistency sentence
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.consistent.summary: The formula Con(T) is the arithmetic sentence ¬□ₜ⊥. It says that no natural number codes a T-proof of contradiction. Its truth in the standard natural numbers expresses ordinary consistency, while the second theorem asks whether T itself can prove that sentence.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.consistent.why_here: Unfolding the definition identifies the sentence that the arithmetic theorem says T cannot prove.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.provable_D.title: Positive introspection
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.provable_D.summary: Positive introspection says that the base theory proves □ₜφ → □ₜ□ₜφ. The existence of a proof code is a Σ₁ assertion. Internal Σ₁-completeness lets the base theory derive the corresponding boxed assertion about T.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.provable_D.why_here: The derivability-conditions step summarizes this theorem when supplying D3.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_complet.title: Represent recursively enumerable predicates
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_complet.summary: For a recursively enumerable predicate D, the representation theorem yields a one-variable formula δ with D(n) exactly when T proves δ at the numeral for n. This is a statement about actual derivability in T. It provides the equivalence that the first theorem later specializes to the code of δ itself.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_complet.why_here: The proof applies the theorem to obtain the numeral-by-numeral representation of D.

lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.göd.title: Gödel sentence specification
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.göd.summary: The diagonal lemma produces a sentence G satisfying a fixed-point equation. The base theory proves G equivalent to the arithmetic assertion that T has no proof of G. The formula G can then be used as an ordinary sentence in arguments both inside and outside the theory.
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.göd.why_here: The Gödel-sentence step summarizes the fixed-point theorem for the chosen provability predicate.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.con.title: Generic consistency unprovability
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.con.summary: The general lemma works with an abstract provability predicate satisfying the required derivability conditions. The base theory proves G equivalent to its associated consistency sentence. A proof of consistency in T would give a proof of G, which consistency rules out.
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.con.why_here: The generic reduction in the graph summarizes this theorem.

fact:presentation.title: Δ₁ presentation
fact:presentation.summary: A Δ₁ presentation makes membership in T’s axiom set definable at the relevant arithmetic complexity. That lets the development encode questions about T-proofs as arithmetic predicates. Both branches use this premise, one to define D and one to build the standard provability predicate.
fact:presentation.why_here: It is a shared input to the coded refutation predicate and the standard provability construction.

fact:r0.title: Arithmetic base R₀
fact:r0.summary: R₀ is the weak arithmetic base in the first theorem. Requiring T to prove its axioms supplies the arithmetic strength used by the representation theorem. The first branch also assumes Σ₁-soundness.
fact:r0.why_here: The representation step uses this base-theory hypothesis.

fact:soundness.title: Σ₁-sound theory
fact:soundness.summary: Σ₁-soundness says that the Σ₁ sentences T proves are true in the standard natural numbers. This gives external consistency. The first proof uses it in its representability setup and invokes the resulting consistency when it rules out both derivations of the witness.
fact:soundness.why_here: It supplies the consistency used to exclude proofs of both sides of the local witness.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

fact:isigma.title: Arithmetic base IΣ₁
fact:isigma.summary: IΣ₁ is the arithmetic base for the second theorem. T proves the axioms of this base, so the fixed-point equivalences and implications established there can be used in T. The base also proves the required derivability conditions for standard provability.
fact:isigma.why_here: It is the base for the standard provability structure, the derivability conditions, and the fixed point.

fact:consistency.title: External consistency
fact:consistency.summary: External consistency means there is no actual T-proof of contradiction. The proof uses this as a hypothesis about T’s derivations. The internal sentence Con(T) is the arithmetic expression whose provability is at issue.
fact:consistency.why_here: It rules out the contradiction that a hypothetical T-proof of G would produce.

step:define-D.title: Code refutation after substitution
step:define-D.summary: Start with the code of a formula φ with one free variable. Substitute the numeral for that very code into φ and ask whether T proves the negation of the resulting sentence. D holds of a code exactly when it codes such a formula and this refutation exists.
step:define-D.why_here: This creates the predicate whose membership will yield refutability at the self-substituted input.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

fact:define-D.title: The predicate D
fact:define-D.summary: For a one-variable formula φ, D at the code of φ is equivalent to the actual provability in T of the negation of φ applied to its own code. This is the branch of the argument that supplies refutability after self-substitution.
fact:define-D.why_here: Its definition is used to establish enumerability and to read off the proof of ¬π in the self-substitution calculation.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

step:enumerate-D.title: Give D a Σ₁ definition
step:enumerate-D.summary: The proof checks arithmetically that the input codes a one-variable formula and performs the coded substitution. It expresses provability of the negated instance as existence of a proof code. The Lean proof establishes a Σ₁ definition and applies the equivalence with recursive enumerability.
step:enumerate-D.why_here: It supplies the enumerability premise needed to represent D.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

fact:enumerate-D.title: D is recursively enumerable
fact:enumerate-D.summary: Recursive enumerability means a search can eventually certify an input for which D holds. It supplies the hypothesis for representing D by provability in T.
fact:enumerate-D.why_here: This is the input passed from the Σ₁-definability argument to the representation theorem.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

step:represent-D.title: Represent D by a formula
step:represent-D.summary: Use recursive enumerability of D to select a one-variable formula δ. The representation theorem yields D(n) exactly when T proves δ with the numeral for n substituted. This gives a second way to read D at any number, including the code of δ.
step:represent-D.why_here: This makes membership in D interchangeable with provability of the corresponding δ instance.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

fact:represent-D.title: Provability represents D
fact:represent-D.summary: For each natural number n, membership in D is equivalent to T-provability of δ at the numeral for n. The equivalence is about provability in the metatheory. The next step takes n to be the code of δ itself.
fact:represent-D.why_here: The next calculation uses the equivalence at the code of δ.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

step:self-substitute.title: Substitute δ’s own code
step:self-substitute.summary: Set π to δ applied to the numeral for δ’s own code. The representation of D says D at that code exactly when T proves π. The definition of D at the same code says exactly when T proves ¬π. Together they make the two provability claims equivalent.
step:self-substitute.why_here: The two interpretations of D at the same number link the positive and negative proof claims.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

fact:self-substitute.title: Opposite provability claims coincide
fact:self-substitute.summary: A T-proof of π would give a T-proof of ¬π, and a T-proof of ¬π would give a T-proof of π. This relates the existence of proofs in the metatheory. The next step uses consistency to rule out both.
fact:self-substitute.why_here: It lets either hypothetical derivation supply its opposite.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

step:exclude-both.title: Rule out both derivations
step:exclude-both.summary: Suppose T proves π. The preceding equivalence then gives a proof of ¬π, and together the two proofs yield a contradiction. Starting with a proof of ¬π gives the same contradiction in the other direction. Hence T proves neither.
step:exclude-both.why_here: This turns the equivalence for the local witness into the two unprovability claims required for incompleteness.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

fact:exclude-both.title: An undecided sentence
fact:exclude-both.summary: π is the particular self-instantiated sentence constructed in the preceding steps. Consistency forbids both its proof and its refutation because either would imply the other. The first incompleteness theorem uses π as the witness for its general existence claim.
fact:exclude-both.why_here: The witness and its two unprovability claims establish the first root.

step:standard-provability.title: Form standard provability
step:standard-provability.summary: Encode formulas and finite T-proofs as natural numbers. Build a predicate expressing that some proof code proves the formula with the given code. Applying it to the code of a sentence φ yields the arithmetic sentence □ₜφ.
step:standard-provability.why_here: It supplies the standard predicate and its initial derivability properties for the arithmetic specialization.

fact:standard-provability.title: Standard provability for T
fact:standard-provability.summary: The same arithmetic predicate is used throughout the second proof. It produces the formula □ₜφ for a sentence φ, the consistency formula at ⊥, and the predicate to which the diagonal lemma is applied.
fact:standard-provability.why_here: The same predicate is used for D3, the consistency sentence, and the Gödel fixed point.

step:hbl-conditions.title: Supply derivability conditions
step:hbl-conditions.summary: D1 internalizes an actual proof. D2 lets arithmetic combine boxed implication and boxed premise by modus ponens. D3 lets arithmetic infer □ₜ□ₜφ from □ₜφ. These are the rules the second proof uses to manipulate proof assertions inside the base theory.
step:hbl-conditions.why_here: The generic internal argument uses the completed structure to reason about iterated proof assertions.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

fact:hbl-conditions.title: Hilbert–Bernays–Löb structure
fact:hbl-conditions.summary: The three conditions govern how □ₜ behaves when reasoning about proofs. The internal argument uses them to derive □ₜ⊥ from □ₜG. The external argument uses D1 to turn a hypothetical proof of G into a proof of its provability.
fact:hbl-conditions.why_here: These conditions let the internal unprovability argument turn □G into □⊥.

step:consistency-sentence.title: Express consistency internally
step:consistency-sentence.summary: Put the code of contradiction ⊥ into the standard provability predicate. Its negation, ¬□ₜ⊥, is an arithmetic sentence saying that there is no code for a T-proof of ⊥. This is the standard Con(T) used in the second theorem.
step:consistency-sentence.why_here: It identifies the arithmetic sentence used as the consistency premise inside the base theory.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

fact:consistency-sentence.title: Internal Con(T)
fact:consistency-sentence.summary: Con(T) is a sentence that T can express. The proof uses it as the premise of an implication proved in the base and later asks whether T can derive Con(T).
fact:consistency-sentence.why_here: The internal implication uses this sentence as its antecedent.

step:godel-sentence.title: Diagonalize the provability predicate
step:godel-sentence.summary: Apply the diagonal lemma to the formula saying that T has no proof of a sentence with a given code. It produces G, for which the base theory proves G ↔ ¬□ₜG. This is the self-reference used in the second theorem.
step:godel-sentence.why_here: The fixed point supplies the connection between G and its coded unprovability used throughout the second argument.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

fact:godel-sentence.title: A Gödel sentence for T
fact:godel-sentence.summary: The base theory proves that G is equivalent to the assertion of its own unprovability in T. From G one can derive ¬□ₜG inside T as well, because T extends the base. This G is the fixed-point sentence used in the second argument.
fact:godel-sentence.why_here: The equivalence is used in the external contradiction, the internal implication, and the comparison with consistency.

step:godel-unprovable.title: Rule out a proof of G
step:godel-unprovable.summary: Assume an actual T-proof of G. D1 gives a proof of □ₜG, while the fixed-point equation and the assumed proof give a proof of ¬□ₜG. Two such proofs contradict the external consistency hypothesis.
step:godel-unprovable.why_here: It supplies the external impossibility needed to rule out a T-proof of consistency.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

fact:godel-unprovable.title: External unprovability of G
fact:godel-unprovable.summary: There is no actual T-proof of G. The last step invokes this metatheoretic fact to rule out a hypothetical T-proof of Con(T).
fact:godel-unprovable.why_here: It contradicts the proof of G that a hypothetical proof of consistency would yield.

step:internal-unprovability.title: Formalize the implication
step:internal-unprovability.summary: Reason inside the base theory and suppose □ₜG. D3 gives □ₜ□ₜG, while internalizing the Gödel equivalence gives boxed evidence that □ₜG implies contradiction. D2 combines them to give □ₜ⊥. Contraposition yields Con(T) → ¬□ₜG inside the base.
step:internal-unprovability.why_here: It provides the direction from internal consistency to the right-hand side of the Gödel equivalence.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

fact:internal-unprovability.title: Internal implication
fact:internal-unprovability.summary: The base proves that its arithmetic assertion Con(T) implies ¬□ₜG. Combining this internal implication with the Gödel equivalence will make Con(T) imply G inside arithmetic.
fact:internal-unprovability.why_here: It provides one direction of the equivalence between Con(T) and ¬□G.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

step:equate-godel-consistency.title: Relate G to consistency
step:equate-godel-consistency.summary: The preceding implication gives Con(T) → ¬□ₜG. In the other direction, any proof of contradiction would give a proof of G, so ¬□ₜG implies Con(T). The fixed-point equation identifies G with ¬□ₜG and closes the equivalence.
step:equate-godel-consistency.why_here: The resulting equivalence allows a proof of consistency to be converted into a proof of G.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

fact:equate-godel-consistency.title: Gödel sentence equivalent to consistency
fact:equate-godel-consistency.summary: The base proves G ↔ Con(T), and T can use this equivalence because it extends the base. The final argument uses its direction from Con(T) to G.
fact:equate-godel-consistency.why_here: It supplies the implication used in the final reduction.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

step:generic-unprovability.title: Reduce a proof of consistency to G
step:generic-unprovability.summary: Suppose T proves the internal sentence Con(T). Since T also proves Con(T) → G by the base-theory equivalence, modus ponens gives a T-proof of G. The previously established external unprovability of G rules this out.
step:generic-unprovability.why_here: It combines the internal equivalence and the external impossibility to obtain generic consistency unprovability.

provenance.author: Source-reviewed explanations and ChatGPT proof roles

fact:generic-unprovability.title: Generic unprovability of consistency
fact:generic-unprovability.summary: For a predicate with the required fixed-point and derivability properties, the generic argument shows that a consistent T cannot prove the associated consistency sentence. The named arithmetic theorem uses the standard arithmetic provability predicate as its instance.
fact:generic-unprovability.why_here: This is the generic conclusion instantiated at the second arithmetic root.
